ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against: Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) sanctions lists; UN Security Council sanctions; EU consolidated financial sanctions and Swiss-autonomous sanctions; OFAC SDN list implemented via Swiss-licensed bank policies for USD clearing; MROS (Money Laundering Reporting Office Switzerland) suspicious activity reporting under AMLA art. 9. Enhanced due diligence applies upon any PEP match or high-risk jurisdiction indicator, including verification of source of wealth and source of funds. Negative news screening and adverse media monitoring are required as best practice for a Low_Risk_Standard manufacturing-retail profile.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – official Central Business Name Index of the Swiss Commercial Register (www.zefix.ch) together with the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered corporate name must be acceptable in at least one official Swiss language (German, French, or Italian). Non-Latin script names require a certified transliteration into Latin characters. The name must contain an indication of the legal form: 'Aktiengesellschaft', 'AG', 'Société Anonyme', 'SA', or 'Società Anonima' as appropriate. The root name must not be misleading, must comply with the rules of truthfulness (Grundsatz der Firmenwahrheit), and must be distinguishable from all existing Swiss trade register names.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Treuhand (in fiduciary context requiring prior supervisory approval)
OECD / UN / World Bank (international organizational names)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a preliminary name examination refusal by the Cantonal Commercial Register Office, the applicant or sponsoring notary must file a reasoned administrative appeal (Einsprache/Beschwerde) with the cantonal commercial register supervisory authority within 30 calendar days of receipt of the written rejection. The appeal must contain: (i) the exact proposed name; (ii) the reason for refusal; (iii) legal arguments citing CO arts. 950–952 and HRegV arts. 19–27; (iv) proposed alternative name in the alternative; and (v) evidence of non-confusing distinctiveness, e.g., trademark or prior-use submissions. A name reservation, once granted, may be renewed once for an additional period of up to 90 days upon notarized request filed before expiry; after expiry, the name loses priority and a new preliminary examination is required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Subject to substance safeguards: A pure letterbox arrangement without any administrative substance is not acceptable for a manufacturing-retail AG under Swiss commercial register practice and may trigger tax reclassification, denial of treaty benefits, and FATF/BEPS scrutiny. Virtual or domiciliation office services by licensed Swiss fiduciaries are permissible only if the company can demonstrate an effective management office, a physical commercial substance threshold relevant to ISIC 3240 (e.g., a warehouse, production facility, or order-fulfillment presence), and full bookkeeping availability in Switzerland. For an online cosplay retail operation targeting Stripe and Shopify Payments, a combination of a domiciliation address and a physical logistics/manufacturing address is strongly recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for a standard low-risk ISIC 3240 profile, estimated at 3–5% probability during the first operational year. Unannounced on-site inspections are possible by cantonal labor authorities, VAT auditors, and anti-undeclared-work task forces if flags arise, such as cash-intensive operations, rapid growth inconsistent with declared substance, anonymous creditor financing, or sanctions-linked supply chains. The likelihood increases materially if UBO or payment-rail patterns trigger enhanced AML monitoring.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR), Arts. 620–763 (Aktiengesellschaft); Art. 626 (incorporation deed), Arts. 629–632 (share capital and paid-up minimum), Art. 716a (inalienable board powers), Art. 643 (registered office); Ordinance on the Commercial Register (HRegV).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug / Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Publicly notarized Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association (Statuten) filed through the cantonal electronic Commercial Register platform
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital is CHF 100,000. At least 20% (CHF 50,000) must be paid up in cash into a designated blocked capital account with a Swiss bank before filing; the balance remains blocked until registration in the Commercial Register is completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the founders' subscription to 1,000 bearer shares, each par value CHF 100, aggregating issued capital of CHF 100,000, is approved, and the paid-up CHF 50,000 (20%) remains blocked in the Swiss capital account until Commercial Register registration is effected. RESOLVED FURTHER that the Articles of Incorporation executed before the notary public are adopted in full; the registered office is fixed at Bahnhofstrasse 15, 6300 Zug, Switzerland. RESOLVED FURTHER that [Founder] is appointed Chairman and Chief Executive Officer with sole signature, [Name] director with collective signature, and the Board is authorized to open the blocked capital account and file the incorporation documents with the Commercial Register of Canton Zug.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Execution of Incorporation Deed and Adoption of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Canton of Zug (Öffentliche Notarin / Notar in Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Zug-licensed civil-law notary; submit the draft German-language Articles of Association; the notary authenticates the founders' identity, reads and executes the public deed of incorporation, and certifies specimen signatures of the directors. The notary then transmits the certified deed set to the Commercial Register portal.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association (Statuten)
Valid passports or identity cards of all founders
Extract from the commercial register and notarized powers of attorney for legal-person founders
Declaration of the registered office address and authorization of the location owner
Certified specimen signatures of each director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary questions clauses or translations, an addendum to the deed is executed and re-notarized; foreign documents otherwise require apostilles and certified German translations before further processing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Capital Account and Capital Payment Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bank licensed in Switzerland with commercial customer desk in Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the future company name with a Swiss bank; deposit at least CHF 50,000 representing the paid-up minimum; instruct the bank to block the funds until Commercial Register registration; obtain the written banker's confirmation (Bankbestätigung) required under Art. 632 OR that the amount is at the bank's free disposal only after registration.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation (draft or execution copy)
List of founders and nominal share allocations
Beneficial ownership declaration (Form X / bank AML collection)
Administration Regulations for banks: natural-person identity records
Draft Commercial Register application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank withholds the deposit confirmation due to incomplete beneficial-ownership data, submit corrected declarations; if the funding standard is unmet, supplement the payment to CHF 50,000 or propose a permitted contribution-in-kind with independent valuation report.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for Entry in the Commercial Register and Official Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug (Commercial Register Office of Canton Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the digitally scanned notarial deed and ancillary declarations through the canton's e-register interface; the registrar checks formal legality, whether capital documentation is proper, and that the legal name contains no confusing third-party marks; upon entry, the registration is published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB) and the company acquires legal personality.
required_dossiers: Public act of incorporation (notarial deed)
Approved Articles of Association
Banker's confirmation of paid-up capital and blocked funds
Declaration of the Board accepting office
Specimen-signature sheet and identity evidence
Completed UID business-identification dataset for the register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar sends interrogatories or requires rectification, file supplementary declarations within 30 days; adverse registration decisions may be appealed to the Cantonal Department of Economic Affairs and ultimately to the Federal Administrative Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Cantonal Fiscal Registration for Tax and Social Security
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Kantonales Steueramt Zug (Cantonal Tax Office of Zug) and Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/UID) with the AHV Compensation Fund (Ausgleichskasse)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the central business identification number (UID) through the federal one-stop shop; the UID issuer automatically opens the VAT account; subsequently register the AG as employer with the competent AHV compensation fund; obtain the cantonal tax number for corporate income and net-worth taxation; sign up for mandatory occupational accident insurance with SUVA via the compensation fund declaration.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register excerpt (post-entry)
Articles of Association and board list
AHV/SUVA employer registration form (F1)
Application for UID allocation (electronic form)
VAT registration information (turnover projection for Art. 91 MWSTG)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the federal UID portal rejects the address or legal-form coding, correct the municipality/Klassifikation fields and resubmit; retroactive taxation statutes apply from the registration date, and delayed UID issuance does not suspend social security obligations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial, Fire-Safety and Occupational Clearance for Textile Production Premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gebäudeversicherung Zug (Canton Zug Building Insurance) with Cantonal Work Safety Inspectorate and SUVA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed production workshop plan to the Cantonal Building Insurance for a mandatory fire-safety inspection against VKF regulations; obtain structural-load certification of the sewing and wig rooms under SIA 261; ensure workstations satisfy Ordinance 3 / ArG ergonomics and safety protocols, and receive the final SUVA accident-insurance policy reference.
required_dossiers: Floor plan with escape routes and fire-behavior designations
Structural engineer's certification of floor load for storage and mannequins
Inventory of synthetic wig cleaning chemicals (e.g., ethanol)
Occupational safety risk assessment (Gefährdungsermittlung)
First-aid and emergency-organization declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the inspection identifies non-compliant fire doors or unsecured shelving, carry out the specified VKF remedies, submit the rectification protocol, and request a re-inspection; commencement of production is stayed only until the clearance certificate is physically delivered.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Trade and Commerce Office of Zug (Amt für Gewerbe und Handel / Zug) with Federal Secretariat for Economic Affairs coordination
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General Commercial Registration Certificate and Industrial Operations Clearance for Textile Tailoring and Synthetic Wig Manufacture

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU/FOEN) with the Environment Office of the Canton of Zug (Amt für Umweltschutz des Kantons Zug)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from mandatory EIA (workshop not listed in Annex 1 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance, UVPV); subject only to cantonal wastewater connection authorization and emission self-monitoring obligations
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: compliance with Art. 7 of the Waters Protection Act (GSchG), discharge into municipal sewer with COD ≤ 25 mg/l and prescribed pH range; volatile organic compounds (VOCs): threshold of 150 mg C/m3 in extract dry exhaust air per Annex 3 of the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV); post-consumer textile waste segregated and disposed through cantonal licensed recycling channels.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Mandatory fire-safety certificate per VKF Brandschutzrichtlinien issued by Gebäudeversicherung Zug; structural load inspection under SIA 261; workplace clearance under the Swiss Labour Act (ArG) and SUVA occupational accident insurance; if the premises encompass bunker-load-bearing civil-defense zones, prior architectural verification by the Cantonal Civil Defense Authority is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni AFC). Official portal: www.estv.admin.ch; Swiss UID Register: www.uid.ch; VAT e-portal: estv.admin.ch (ePortal TVA/MWST).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Articles of incorporation and notarial deed filed with the Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt); issuance of the Swiss UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer, format CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx) is automatic upon registration and serves as the universal federal/cantonal tax identification number. 2. The cantonal tax administration opens the corporate income tax and capital tax file for the AG upon commercial registration; declaration of tax residence is based on statutory seat and place of effective management. 3. VAT registration: the company must register for Swiss VAT with the ESTV within 30 days after exceeding CHF 100,000 of worldwide taxable turnover (exclusive of VAT); registration is executed through the ESTV electronic portal (ePortal TVA); the VAT identification number consists of the UID plus the suffix 'MWST' (e.g., CHE-123.456.789 MWST). 4. Non-resident entities supplying goods or services with Swiss nexus must apply directly to the ESTV using Form 1062 'Registration for VAT Purposes' and appoint a Swiss tax representative for service of process and VAT compliance. 5. The AG must separately register as a paying agent with the ESTV for Swiss withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) before distributing dividends or other payments subject to 35% WHT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. Swiss AG is a resident taxpayer under the classical corporate tax system: unlimited tax liability on worldwide income (Direct Federal Tax Act DBG Art. 50; tax harmonization laws apply cantonal/communal levels), with relief for foreign permanent establishments and foreign real estate under the exemption method (cantonal) or credit method (federal). Federal corporate income tax of 8.5% plus cantonal/communal income and capital taxes (aggregate effective rate typically 11%–21% depending on canton; Zug/Zugerberg rates circa 11.9%). Distributions are subject to 35% Swiss withholding tax, refundable in whole or in part under applicable treaty or domestic restitution rules. The AG is not a pass-through entity; no entity-level tax exemption applies in the standard regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Swiss tax law. Available statutory elections relevant to this entity: (1) Voluntary VAT registration under Art. 11 Federal Act on Value Added Tax (MWSTG) for persons exempt from tax liability on turnover not exceeding CHF 100,000. (2) VAT group taxation election (Organschaft) under Art. 21 MWSTG, allowing closely controlled legal entities to be treated as a single taxpayer with consolidated VAT reporting and internal supplies outside the scope of VAT. (3) Participation deduction election (Art. 69/70 federal; cantonal equivalents) for dividends and capital gains from qualifying participations. (4) Hybrid mismatch rules implementing BEPS Action 2 apply mandatorily since 1 January 2020 with no elective carve-out; where a hybrid instrument or entity produces a deduction-without-inclusion outcome, the federal tax administration (FTA Circular No. 32) aligns treatment by denying the deduction.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / TVA / Imposta sul valore aggiunto)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 worldwide annual taxable turnover (exclusive of VAT; Art. 10 para. 2 MWSTG). Turnover below this threshold is exempt from tax liability on a mandatory basis, subject to voluntary registration. Special thresholds and simplified flat-rate methods may apply to non-resident digital suppliers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, no government-approved API digital stamping, and no continuous transaction control in Switzerland. Invoicing is governed by Art. 26 MWSTG, requiring the invoice to identify supplier and recipient (name and address), the supplier's UID, invoice date, description of goods/services, consideration, applicable VAT rate and tax amount; failure to include VAT in compliant form shifts the tax liability. Electronic invoicing is permitted on B2B and B2C with recipient consent; voluntary standards include the SIX eBill framework and the Peppol BIS-CH network. The Swiss Federal Administration is progressively introducing PEPPOL-based e-invoicing for public procurement suppliers, but no statutory private-sector e-invoicing mandate is currently in force. Statutory retention of invoices and export evidence: 10 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating for export of goods under Art. 23 para. 1 MWSTG applies where the cosplay prop apparel, theatrical costume robes, and synthetic wigs are physically transported to a foreign destination (outside Switzerland, including the Principality of Liechtenstein under the Swiss-Liechtenstein VAT treaty) by the supplier, the recipient, or a third party carrier. The supplier must obtain adequate documentary proof of export before the expiration of the legal assessment period; transport and export must be evidenced by customs exit confirmation from Swiss customs (e-dec process) or, for goods supplied to customers in EU/EEA states, by the export declaration together with transport documentation. Services closely connected to exported goods and certain services supplied to foreign recipients may also qualify for zero-rating under Art. 23 para. 2 MWSTG. The supplying AG should maintain the export evidence in the order of the shipment for immediate production to the ESTV upon request.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Official Swiss customs export declaration (e-dec / Ausfuhranmeldung) with electronic customs exit certification and transit evidence from Swiss Customs Administration (OZD).

Transport document proving physical departure from Switzerland: Bill of Lading (sea), Air Waybill (air), CMR consignment note (road), postal/courier customs declaration for low-value parcels, or Swiss Customs exit stamp.

Commercial invoice (original) referencing the exporter's Swiss UID/MWST number, describing the goods, stating the delivery terms (Incoterms), and confirming the Israel? none; stating the consideration; non-dated.

Inward remittance certificate or SWIFT/MT103 bank confirmation evidencing receipt of export proceeds in the company's Swiss bank account (employed as a supporting audit-trail document for standard 180-day repatriation review).

For goods exported via an EU intermediary: the recipient or customs agent confirmation of importation in the country of destination or the EU electronic transit record (NCTS) referencing the Swiss export declaration.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Swiss law does not impose a statutory foreign exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds; however, the 180-day benchmark is applied by the ESTV as a prudent evidentiary window for receipt of export consideration. Export zero-rating is subject to retroactive reclassification if the documentary proof is incomplete or untruthful: the supply is treated as a taxable domestic supply at the standard 8.1% rate, with interest on the additional tax due at 4.5% per annum. Penalty provisions of the Swiss VAT Act (MWSTG): Art. 95 - tax evasion penalty up to four times the tax evaded; Art. 96 - criminal fraud (Leistungsbetrug) with imprisonment up to ten years for intentional schemes; Art. 98 - procedural violation fines up to CHF 50,000 in serious cases; limitation periods of 5 years generally and 10 years in cases of tax evasion (Art. 42/43 MWSTG). Customs law parallel sanctions apply for false export declarations under the Federal Customs Act. Companies operating via Stripe or Shopify Payments should reconcile payment-rail settlement records with export documentation to preempt nexus-based audits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) / Swiss Federal Department of Finance's State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) for sanctions and financial market regulation
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full convertibility for both current and capital account transactions under the free movement of capital enshrined in the Swiss Federal Constitution and OECD liberalisation codes. No prior exchange control approval is required for inbound equity, shareholder loans, trade settlements, or profit remittances. Dividends, royalties, interest, and liquidation proceeds may be freely transferred abroad, subject only to Swiss withholding tax of 35% on qualifying distributions, which may be reduced or refunded under applicable double taxation treaties. Banking relation risk is not FX regulatory but counterparty compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland imposes no statutory surrender obligation or mandatory conversion timeline for export proceeds. Exporters may hold, invest, or disburse foreign currency receipts freely. For manufacturing sales of cosplay props/apparel, there is no FX surrender ratio, no declaration threshold for routine current-account receipts, and no requirement to route through a designated local bank, although bank account opening requires compliance with the Due Diligence Ordinance (VSB 20) and Anti-Money Laundering Act.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with SIC and Target2/SWIFT USD clearing
Operational Account / Standard CHF Business Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium feasibility. Under FinIA and FinSA, non-Swiss digital EMI passporting does not exist under an EU PSD-equivalent regime. Offshore EMI-only accounts are legally constrained because they lack Swiss SIC membership and cannot directly settle CHF; they require interoperability through a Swiss licensed bank sponsor. For a low-risk cosplay apparel manufacturer, a FINMA-licensed neobank or banking-as-a-service solution with UBS/ZKB is viable, whereas a pure unregulated offshore EMI account will generally be rejected as an invalid deposit-taking vehicle and cannot support corporate payroll, VAT refunds, or commercial LC issuance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Major Swiss banks typically allow remote video identification for a low-risk Swiss AG, but operational AML practice frequently requires at least one authorised signatory with Swiss residence. For non-resident directors, a physical appearance at a Swiss bank branch or notary is generally mandated for first onboarding; remote opening is possible only where the bank has an existing relationship, a Swiss-chartered signatory (Prokurist), or a regulated Swiss trustee is appointed. The underwriter retains absolute discretion, and cantonal banks often require notarially certified passport/reference documents plus video confirmation with the UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO / director with no Swiss nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passport and residence permit certified by Swiss notary or Swiss embassy; detailed curriculum vitae and business background; proof of Swiss registered office or warehouse; audited prior financial statements; evidence of local accountant and payroll agent appointment; explicit written commercial rationale for establishing the Swiss AG.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions screening hit or adverse media on UBO or intermediary
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Individual and corporate criminal record certificates from all prior countries of residence; PEP status declaration; tax residence certificates; signed source-of-wealth statement; two independent bank reference letters; adverse media explanation memorandum with supporting transactional evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of injected capital for a newly formed Aktiengesellschaft
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Swiss notary deed with capital contribution certificate (Geldbericht / detailed funds statement); bank confirmation of payment into the blocked capital account; 12-month bank statements and transaction listings evidencing the UBO's source of funds; valuation documentation if the contribution is made in kind.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business model mismatch between registered purpose and actual high-volume online retail sales
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated Commercial Register extract; detailed business plan for cosplay prop and costume manufacture; e-commerce platform contracts (Stripe, Shopify Payments); supplier and logistics agreements; product liability insurance certificate; expected annual turnover and transaction volume statement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing uses a same-name wire from the UBO's existing bank to the Swiss SIC-member bank. CHF transfers settle via SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing) with purpose code 'S10 – Others/Capital Contribution' or 'INVE – Direct Investment'; EUR/CHF settle via Target2-SWISS euro clearing; USD transfers settle via SWIFT MT103/202 through a US correspondent. Verification documents include notarised Articles of Association, capital payment confirmation from the bank's notary, and, for shareholder loans, a signed loan agreement with arm's length interest and subordination statement. Forbidden payment language includes 'investment funds', 'portfolio management', or 'lending', which trigger additional FinIA/AMLA review.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Domestic CHF supplier payments clear through SIC. EUR payments clear through SEPA Instant or Target2. Cross-border USD/EUR/CHF trade settlements use SWIFT MT103; for larger equipment or bulk fabric purchases, commercial letters of credit under UCP600 are issued via the Swiss relationship bank. For outbound trade disbursements, use purpose code 'Purchase of goods' with invoice, packing list, customs declaration, and transport documents on file. For Stripe/Shopify Payments fees and SaaS subscriptions, use SEPA direct debit or MT103 with the applicable treasury purpose code and the underlying merchant agreement as supporting evidence.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla OTC FX forwards in CHF/EUR/USD with Swiss-regulated commercial banks
Onshore deliverable forward contracts executed with FINMA-supervised Swiss banks
Cross-currency interest rate swaps to hedge foreign-currency shareholder loans with documented hedge intent
FX options (call/put) under ISDA documentation for hedging forecast trade receivables
No NDF market exists for the Swiss franc; NDFs are not a permitted hedging route unless executed with a non-Swiss bank and documented offshore with strict hedging intent

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual commercial register data confirmation (Registerbestätigung / confirmation des données du registre)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Once per calendar year within one month after the annual shareholders' meeting; the shareholders' meeting must be held within six months after the balance-sheet date (by 30 June for a 31 December year-end).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Cantonal register office may issue a reminder and impose administrative fines; continued failure to maintain accurate registered data can lead to a formal court request and ultimately ex officio strike-off of the inactive legal entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements, appropriation of profit, and discharge resolutions approved and minuted at the Annual General Meeting (AGM)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Annual General Meeting of shareholders and the Board of Directors (corporate minutes and records)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be convened within six months from the balance-sheet date under Art. 699 Swiss Code of Obligations; for a calendar-year entity, the practical deadline is 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A shareholder may petition the competent court to convene or conduct the AGM; if the board fails to act, directors may incur personal liability for resulting losses and statutory fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Swiss federal and cantonal corporate income tax return (including profit tax, capital tax, and federal tax schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (Kantonales Steueramt) and Federal Tax Administration (ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Usually 31 March following the tax year, with the principal canton normally granting an extension to 30 June; the exact deadline depends on the seat canton.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers penalty interest on assessed federal and cantonal taxes; procedural fines may be imposed, and deliberate misstatements are prosecuted as tax evasion under Swiss federal and cantonal tax statutes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Swiss VAT return (MWST-Abrechnung / décompte TVA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV / AFD), Swiss VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For enterprises authorized to report annually, the return is due within 60 days after the close of the fiscal year; quarterly filers must file within 60 days after each quarter-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty interest applies to unpaid VAT; the Federal Tax Administration may impose administrative fines for late or inaccurate returns, and deliberate VAT evasion is subject to criminal penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An ordinary audit is compulsory when the AG exceeds two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total above CHF 20 million, turnover above CHF 40 million, and an annual average of more than 250 full-time employees. If an ordinary audit is not triggered, a limited audit (review engagement) is required unless the shareholders unanimously exercise the statutory opting-out right under Art. 727a OR, available only when the company averages fewer than 10 full-time employees per year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR), Arts. 957–963a; Swiss GAAP FER is the widely accepted framework for non-listed AGs; IFRS Accounting Standards are mandatory for listed equity issuers and for the consolidated financial statements of listed Swiss parent companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law does not require a separate public annual beneficial-ownership return for private AGs. Beneficial-ownership information is provided to Swiss financial intermediaries, tax authorities, or auditors on an ad hoc due-diligence basis; the commercial register confirmation contains corporate details and signatory powers, not private UBO data. The AG must keep its share register and board records continuously current and file changes with the cantonal commercial register within the applicable 14-day change-reporting period.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Shareholders (Aktienbuch / registre des actions)
Register of Directors and Executive Signatories (board and managing-director records)
Minute Book (protocols of shareholders' meetings and board meetings)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$ 2,000 – US$ 10,000 for a limited audit; US$ 15,000 – US$ 40,000+ for a full ordinary audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal corporate income tax (statutory rate; effective federal rate is 7.83% because the federal tax itself is deductible); in the target Zug/Crypto-Valley location the combined federal, cantonal and communal ordinary effective headline rate is approximately 11.9%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory participation exemption (100% exemption on qualifying dividend and capital-gain income from participations of at least 10% held for at least one year); cantonal patent box (up to 90% exemption of qualifying patent/IP income); R&D super-deduction of up to 150% in adopting cantons; notional interest deduction available in certain cantons; no Swiss federal group relief.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal and cantonal corporate income tax declaration for legal entities ('Steuererklärung juristische Personen'), comprising the federal tax schedule and the cantonal schedule; e-filing is conducted through the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) e-Filing portal and the respective cantonal portal (Zug: 'TaxMe' / Online-Steuererklärung for AGs).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The tax return must be filed within 30 days of service of the return form; forms are ordinarily issued by the cantonal tax administration after the annual financial statements are approved, typically within six months after the fiscal year-end. Ordinary extensions are granted to 30 September following the tax year-end; non-filing triggers a formal reminder, then estimated assessment by the tax authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of the exact 12-month fiscal period covered by the commercial balance sheet.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned Swiss AG: file on a standalone, tax-book basis; no consolidation or tax-group attribution of the non-resident shareholder is permitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net commercial profit after deduction of operating expenses and before tax reconciliation adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply transfer pricing corrections to management, royalty, interest and service fees paid to the non-resident parent; add back non-deductible items including hidden profit distributions and excessive director remuneration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividends, liquidation surplus and capital gains from qualifying participations claimed for the participation exemption.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Swiss AG must document a minimum 10% participation and a 12-month holding period; passive portfolio dividends below the threshold are fully taxable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of prior-year tax loss carry-forwards against current-year taxable profit; legal carry-forward period is seven years, no carry-back available.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses realized by the non-resident shareholder or by the Swiss AG in a foreign permanent establishment cannot be transferred or offset in the Swiss AG.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9d / Ausländische Betriebsstätte und ausländische Immobilien
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exemption of foreign permanent-establishment profits and foreign real property income from the Swiss assessment base under Art. 52 DBG and the applicable DTA.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide full double-tax relief calculations and PE documentation; the Swiss AG remains taxable on worldwide income where no exemption claim is established.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of gross dividend distributions and the 35% federal withholding tax collected from shareholders and remitted to ESTV.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must file Form VSt-82 with the Swiss tax authority to obtain relief at source or a refund of the treaty-reduced portion, attaching a valid tax residency certificate and beneficial-ownership declaration.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a procedural fine (Ordnungsbusse) of up to CHF 1,000 under Art. 174 DBG, with cantonal fines up to CHF 10,000; the authorities may assess estimated taxable profit with default interest of 4.5% per annum. Intentional under-declaration is sanctioned with a fine of up to three times the evaded federal tax (Art. 175 DBG); falsification of accounts constitutes tax fraud punishable under Art. 186 DBG with imprisonment or additional monetary penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) imposed on all gross dividend distributions by the Swiss AG; the 35% deduction is final for Swiss-resident individuals but refundable or reducible to treaty rates for non-resident shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must (1) obtain a tax residency certificate from its home tax administration, (2) submit Form VSt-82 before distribution for relief at source, or alternatively claim a refund from ESTV within three years of the distribution date (Art. 32 VStG), (3) provide a beneficial-ownership statement and evidence of holding period. Typical DTA rates: 15% for portfolio holdings and 5% for qualifying corporate holdings of at least 10%; treaty benefits are denied if the shareholder fails economic-substance or limitation-on-benefits conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: Swiss statutory withholding tax rate is 0% — Switzerland does not impose source withholding tax on cross-border licence or IP royalty payments, so DTA royalty rates are inapplicable. Interest: Swiss statutory withholding tax is 0% on arm's length commercial-loan interest paid to non-resident lenders; a 35% WHT applies only to public bond interest and to bank interest paid to Swiss-resident recipients. Excessive interest recharacterized as constructive equity under Swiss thin-capitalisation practice is treated as a dividend subject to 35% WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File documentation is required where annual cross-border related-party goods or service transactions exceed CHF 5 million; Master File documentation is required for multinational groups with consolidated gross revenue of at least CHF 80 million; Country-by-Country reporting is mandatory for groups with consolidated revenue of CHF 900 million or more. Regardless of thresholds, the Swiss AG must produce contemporaneous arm's length documentation within 60 days of an ESTV request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not maintain a codified Economic Substance Regulations regime, but applies the economic-reality principle and substance-over-form doctrine (Art. 2 DBG and Federal Tax Administration circular practice). The Swiss AG must demonstrate real local substance — board meetings held in Switzerland, locally resident management and qualified staff, commercial premises, actual business decision-making and risk-bearing capacity — to sustain participation exemption, patent box relief, DTA treaty benefits and any ruling of the Zug tax authority; letterbox shell structures are reassessed, denied relief and exposed to full taxation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Statements (Steuerhinterziehung / Steuerbetrug)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly under-declaring Stripe/Shopify gross receipts or cash cosplay-apparel sales, fabricating supplier invoices, or inflating deductible expenses to reduce Swiss taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Federal sanction: additional tax equal to the evaded amount plus a fine of up to three times the evaded federal tax (Art. 175 DBG); tax fraud committed by falsifying books, registers or using counterfeit documents is punished with imprisonment of up to three years and ancillary financial penalties (Art. 186 DBG), with publication of the judgment and confiscation of illegal profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, de-facto managers and signatories are individually prosecuted; personal imprisonment, board disqualification, and civil damages under Art. 754 OR may be imposed. Swiss criminal procedure allows seizure of private assets, security for the tax claim and a travel ban (Ausreiseverbot, Art. 239 ff. StPO) where flight risk exists; the corporate veil is pierced when directors have used the AG as a mere instrument of personal enrichment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends, constructive profit distributions, director current-account benefits or excessive management fees without withholding the 35% federal tax, or failing to remit the withheld amount to ESTV within the statutory quarterly declaration cycle.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ESTV enforces payment of the full 35% against the Swiss AG without time limitation (Art. 14 VStG), plus default interest at 5% per annum and a fine of up to CHF 5,000 per offense; the unpaid WHT blocks any treaty refund for the non-resident shareholder.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members are jointly and severally personally liable for uncollected or unremitted withholding tax when the company is insolvent (Art. 12 VStG); direct enforcement against personal assets, criminal fines and coercive measures including travel bans apply to finance-responsible directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Thin Capitalisation (Gewinnverlagerung / Konstruktive Dividende)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying non-arm's length royalties, management fees, interest or service charges to a non-resident parent, or maintaining intercompany debt exceeding Swiss thin-capitalisation safe harbours (roughly 60%–70% debt-to-asset value) without commercial purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-assessment of the Swiss AG with add-back of the excess expenses to taxable profit, default interest, and potential penalty; the recharacterized amount is treated as a constructive dividend subject to 35% withholding tax; incomplete documentation can trigger fines of up to CHF 10,000 and estimated assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and controlling shareholders who arrange abusive intercompany pricing are jointly liable for the additional corporate tax and the 35% WHT (Art. 12 VStG and Art. 57 DBG); documented deliberate evasion leads to personal criminal prosecution, imprisonment, forfeiture of assets and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Abuse and AML Violations (Geldwäscherei / Mangelhafte Sorgfalt)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Swiss AG as an empty letterbox with no genuine cosplay-production, tailoring or retail activity, or using Stripe, Shopify Payments or third-party payout accounts to move funds to undisclosed beneficial owners or sanctioned counterparties while concealing the true economic interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering is punishable by up to three years' imprisonment and/or a fine of up to CHF 500,000 (Art. 305bis CP); negligent failure in financial due diligence is punishable by a fine of up to CHF 500,000 (Art. 305ter CP); all illicit proceeds are subject to confiscation (Art. 70 CP); the tax administration will annul all planning benefits and reassess hidden distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners face personal criminal conviction, civil restitution to creditors, worldwide asset freezes and travel bans imposed under the Swiss Code of Criminal Procedure; the corporate veil is pierced and personal assets are forfeited where the AG is operated as a sham.
